summary_paragraph: A man with nonischemic cardiomyopathy, type 1 diabetes, and a history of cocaine dependence was admitted for acute shortness of breath and chest pain following crack use. Initially managed for heart failure with diuresis and vasodilators, his respiratory status improved with BiPAP and fluid removal. Imaging revealed diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities, with a pattern suggesting crack-induced lung injury or hypersensitivity pneumonitis rather than infection or pure pulmonary edema. He was treated with a single dose of steroids, which caused transient hyperglycemia managed with an insulin drip before returning to home insulin. Antibiotics were avoided due to lack of infection evidence. He weaned successfully from oxygen, stabilized on home heart and diabetes medications, and was discharged with instructions to avoid illicit substances, continue all medications, and follow up for addiction support and hepatitis C monitoring.
problems: Acute pulmonary syndrome (presumably related to crack-cocaine use)
Acute on chronic exacerbation of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy
